correctness.rationale: Latent centered-state conditional expectation gives Cov(Z_i,Z_j)=A lambda^(j-i) and the centered third moment A(1-2pi)lambda^2. Conditional observation independence multiplies by positive contrasts. R=1/A-4, covariance ratio fixes signed lambda, and explicit positive square roots determine all eight emission rates and both transitions uniquely, including lambda<0 and pi=1/2. The three-season reparametrization lambda to nearby lambda prime scales the two outer contrasts and preserves exactly the seven moments determining the whole three-bit law. An exact rational standalone verifier exhaustively computes all 16 observed histories in four test cases and an eight-history nonidentifiability witness. A finite test does not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Unknown false detections and false negatives with changing survey effort are important for repeated ecological monitoring. The theorem gives a precise minimum number of single-visit seasons, an algebraically explicit low-order-moment inverse for all ecological transition and survey-error rates, and a rigorous continuous nonidentifiability obstruction below the cutoff. This is a structural survey-design boundary, not merely numerical parameter fitting or an arbitrary finite slice; it clarifies when repeated within-season visits are mathematically unnecessary under strong stationarity conditions while warning about instability.
